hotel.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 13:00. Take the Magical Express or budget shuttle (Mears Connect from ~$16/person one-way) to your boutique stay near Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Pick up a Disney park map and review your week's game plan. Walk around the Disney Springs area (free admission) to soak in the atmosphere, browse shops, and enjoy the lively entertainment district along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your first evening exploring Disney Springs fully — it's free to enter and offers world-class people-watching, street performers, and live music at no cost. Window-shop at the LEGO Store, check out the giant Christmas shop, and enjoy the festive Disney atmosphere as a gentle intro to the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during your flight to save money on arrival day.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or pack snacks for the shuttle ride. Budget tip: stop at a Publix or Walmart near the resort to stock up on breakfast items, snacks, and drinks for the week (~$30-40 investment that saves big daily).
meals.dinner: Disney Springs - Blaze Pizza offers fast, customizable pizzas for around $10-12 per person. Alternatively, Earl of Sandwich has hearty sandwiches for $8-10. Both are wallet-friendly compared to most Disney dining options.

day_by_day.notes: Priority on arrival day: Visit a nearby Publix (use Lyft or hotel shuttle, ~10 min away) to buy bottled water, granola bars, fruit, and easy breakfast items. Bringing your own snacks and drinks into the parks saves $20-40 per day. Refillable water bottles are a must — Disney offers free ice water at any quick-service counter. Download the My Disney Experience app tonight to check wait times and plan park days.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and head to Magic Kingdom — the crown jewel of Walt Disney World. Arrive at rope drop (park opening, typically 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then loop to Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train (use Individual Lightning Lane if budget allows, ~$15-20, or ride at rope drop when lines are shortest). Explore Cinderella Castle and take iconic photos. Hit Peter Pan's Flight and The Haunted Mansion before mid-morning crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, head to Adventureland for Pirates of the Caribbean (low wait times post-lunch) and the Jungle Cruise. Explore Liberty Square and catch the Hall of Presidents. Use the hottest part of the afternoon (2-4 PM) to revisit air-conditioned attractions or take a short break. Ride Big Thunder Mountain Railroad in Frontierland and browse the shops along Main Street U.S.A.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Magic Kingdom nighttime spectacular — Happily Ever After fireworks display (check current schedule on the app). This is completely included with park admission and is one of the most breathtaking shows at any theme park in the world. Watch from the hub in front of Cinderella Castle for the best view. Exit after the fireworks via the free Disney bus back to your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Eat your pre-purchased groceries at the hotel before heading out — yogurt, fruit, and granola bars keep costs down and energy up.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square offers clam chowder, fish and chips, and chicken sandwiches for $12-15 per entree. It's often overlooked and less crowded than Main Street options. Split a larger meal if dining with family.
meals.dinner: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn & Cafe in Frontierland — burgers, nachos, and rice bowls for $12-15. The unlimited toppings bar (lettuce, tomatoes, sautéed peppers, onions) stretches your meal significantly. Eat dinner before 5:30 PM to avoid peak dinner wait times.

day_by_day.notes: Magic Kingdom tips: Download the My Disney Experience app and check Lightning Lane availability first thing in the morning. Free standby lines are manageable at rope drop and after 8 PM. Bring your refillable water bottle — free ice water is available at any quick-service location just by asking. Wear comfortable shoes; expect 8-12 miles of walking. June weather in Orlando is hot and humid (88-95°F) with afternoon thunderstorms common — pack a small poncho ($1-2 at Dollar Tree vs. $12 in-park).

day_by_day.morning: Head to EPCOT at rope drop. Start in World Discovery (formerly Future World) — ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue, free, open at 7 AM on the app — join immediately upon waking). Then experience Test Track and Mission: SPACE. Explore the stunning new EPCOT center area and the iconic geodesic Spaceship Earth attraction (a classic, gentle ride great for all ages).
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to World Showcase, which opens at 11 AM. Walk the 1.2-mile promenade around World Showcase Lagoon visiting pavilions from 11 countries. Each pavilion has free entertainment, cultural exhibits, and unique architecture. Stop in the Norway pavilion for Frozen Ever After (moderate wait times in the afternoon). Explore the Morocco, Japan, and China pavilions for free cultural entertainment and beautiful architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT Forever or the current nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon — included with park admission and absolutely stunning. Watch from the Canada or UK pavilion side for a great, less-crowded vantage point. Take the free Disney Skyliner gondola back toward your hotel area for a unique and scenic ride.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast from your grocery haul — instant oatmeal, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: EPCOT's World Showcase is famous for international food booths and kiosks. Visit the Mexico pavilion for a budget-friendly taco or the American Adventure for a hot dog or turkey leg (~$10-14). The Food & Wine Festival (if running in June) offers small plates from $4-8 each — ideal for budget sampling.
meals.dinner: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — one of EPCOT's best quick-service spots with rotisserie chicken, Asian noodle bowls, and sandwiches for $12-15. It's large, air-conditioned, and less crowded than World Showcase restaurants. Alternatively, grab a School Bread ($5) and snacks from the Norway bakery as a lighter dinner option.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT budget tip: The World Showcase pavilions are loaded with free entertainment — the Bijutsu-kan Gallery in Japan, the Stave Church in Norway, and the American Adventure film are all no-cost highlights. Drinking around the world (sampling beverages from each country) is popular but costs add up fast — budget $5-8 per drink if you choose to participate. The free Kidcot Fun Stops in each pavilion are great for kids and include a free craft activity.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Hollywood Studios at rope drop. This park requires strategic planning. Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — join the virtual queue or Individual Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance (the most popular attraction at Walt Disney World, ~$20-25 per person via Lightning Lane or free via virtual queue on the app at park open). While waiting, ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run in standby (30-45 min at rope drop). Explore the immersive Galaxy's Edge land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Toy Story Land — Slinky Dog Dash roller coaster is best in the morning but manageable in early afternoon. Alien Swirling Saucers is fun for younger guests. Walk over to the Animation Courtyard for Star Wars Launch Bay (free exhibits and character meet-and-greets). Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (check schedule on app) — it's free with park admission and genuinely impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Experience The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith in the late afternoon when lines typically drop. Stay for Fantasmic! — the nighttime water, fire, and projection show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater. It's included with park admission and is one of Disney's best live shows. Arrive 45-60 minutes early for good seating.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast from grocery supplies before rope drop.
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — grilled cheese sandwiches, BBQ brisket melts, and totchos (tater tot nachos) for $10-14. It's a beloved quick-service spot with reasonable prices for a Disney park.
meals.dinner: ABC Commissary — one of Hollywood Studios' most budget-friendly quick-service options with burgers, wraps, and Mediterranean bowls for $12-15. Large portions and a cool, air-conditioned space. Eat at 5 PM before the Fantasmic! dinner rush.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most attraction-dense park per square foot. The Lightning Lane Multi Pass (~$25-30/person/day) is worth considering here more than other parks given the high demand for Rise of the Resistance. Budget alternative: join the free virtual queue at 7 AM sharp on the My Disney Experience app — spots go fast. Wear your most comfortable shoes as the park involves significant walking between themed lands.

day_by_day.morning: Start at Animal Kingdom at rope drop. Head directly to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (the most in-demand ride in the park — standby waits reach 120+ minutes by mid-morning). Rope drop is your best bet for a 20-30 minute wait. Then ride Na'vi River Journey next door. Explore the bioluminescent beauty of Pandora's landscape — even the theming alone is worth the visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pandora, explore Africa — ride Kilimanjaro Safaris (best in the morning for active animals, but afternoon works too). Walk the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for free wildlife viewing. Head to Asia for Expedition Everest — one of Disney's best roller coasters — and Kali River Rapids (you WILL get wet — plan accordingly or skip if you don't want soaked clothes). Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks (6-8 PM), so plan to finish by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel by late afternoon for a well-deserved rest day. Use the hotel pool if available. Head to Disney Springs in the evening for free entertainment, live music, and a relaxed browse. This is a great evening to recharge before your final full park day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — keep it light before a hot park day.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — widely regarded as one of the best quick-service restaurants at Walt Disney World. Grain bowls, protein options, and unique Avatar-themed dishes for $13-16. The Cheeseburger Steamed Pods and Blueberry Cream Cheese Mousse are fan favorites.
meals.dinner: Disney Springs dinner — Chicken Guy! by Guy Fieri offers crispy chicken tenders with 22 sauces for around $10-13. Fun, casual, and budget-friendly. Or grab a Ghirardelli sundae for a sweet treat to celebrate the halfway point of your trip.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom tip: The Tree of Life is stunning and worth a slow walk-around to spot the 325 animals carved into its trunk. The Finding Nemo: The Big Blue... and Beyond! show (check if running) is a lovely, air-conditioned break. June afternoons bring heavy thunderstorms in Orlando — Animal Kingdom has less indoor shelter than other parks, so keep an eye on the weather app and plan accordingly. Your Dollar Tree poncho will earn its keep today.

day_by_day.morning: Use this day as a flexible park-hopping day if your ticket includes that option, or revisit your favorite park from the week. Recommended: Return to Magic Kingdom for any missed attractions or to re-ride favorites with potentially shorter waits mid-week. Alternatively, use the morning to revisit EPCOT's World Showcase at a slower pace and explore pavilions you rushed through earlier.
day_by_day.afternoon: If park hopping, head to a second park in the afternoon (park hopping is allowed after 2 PM on most Disney tickets). Alternatively, spend the afternoon at your hotel pool — a great budget option that requires no extra spending. Many Disney resort pools have waterslides and themed areas that are genuinely fun. Use this downtime to do souvenir shopping at Disney Springs (more affordable than in-park shops) and pick up any last gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner tonight as a trip celebration — or keep it budget-friendly with a picnic-style meal from your grocery supplies back at the hotel. Head to Disney Springs for the free outdoor concerts and entertainment that typically run on weekend evenings. Enjoy a final leisurely evening stroll along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — use up remaining grocery supplies to minimize waste before departure tomorrow.
meals.lunch: Quick-service meal at whichever park you visit — aim for $12-15 per person. Look for kids' meals if traveling with children ($7-9 and often surprisingly filling).
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — slightly upscale but with appetizers and lighter entrees in the $15-22 range. Share a few appetizers as a family for a more affordable experience. Or keep it budget-friendly with another round at Blaze Pizza or Earl of Sandwich.

day_by_day.notes: Souvenir budget tip: Disney Springs shops have the same merchandise as in-park stores but without the impulse-buy pressure. Set a firm souvenir budget at the start of the trip ($20-30 per person) and stick to it. The $1-3 pressed penny machines throughout all parks are a beloved, budget-friendly collectible tradition. Check if your hotel offers any complimentary activities or entertainment tonight — boutique stays near Disney sometimes have movie nights or pool events.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final morning. Check out of your boutique stay (confirm checkout time — typically 11 AM). If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, store luggage with the front desk and spend a few final hours at Disney Springs for last-minute souvenir shopping, photos, and a nostalgic farewell stroll. Grab a Mickey-shaped treat as a final Disney memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange your airport transfer — book Mears Connect or a rideshare (Uber/Lyft typically $30-45 to Orlando International Airport) in advance. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for travel time and airport security. Orlando International Airport has good food options post-security if you need a final meal before flying.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Orlando with magical memories, a camera full of photos, and hopefully some money still in your wallet! Review your My Disney Experience app for any downloadable PhotoPass memories from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Use remaining hotel grocery supplies for a final in-room breakfast — finish off any remaining snacks, fruit, and drinks to avoid waste.
meals.lunch: Disney Springs — grab a quick and affordable farewell lunch. Chicken Guy!, Earl of Sandwich, or a food kiosk snack for $10-12. Keep it light before travel.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on your departure time and flight details.

day_by_day.notes: Departure day tips: Pack all souvenirs carefully and check airline baggage weight limits to avoid fees. Take a final photo at the Disney Springs waterfront as a trip memento. Total estimated budget summary for 7 days: Park tickets ($400-600/person for 4-day tickets + free days at Disney Springs), food ($30-50/day with grocery supplementation), transportation ($60-80 round trip airport transfers), souvenirs ($50-100 total). Staying disciplined with in-room breakfasts and snacks, free Disney Springs evenings, and smart park timing can keep a family of 4 trip under $3,000-3,500 total excluding flights and hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use the time to collect luggage, arrange Disney's Magical Express or a rideshare to your Boutique Stay in Magic Kingdom/Lake Buena Vista, and get settled into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Pool Time — After checking in, explore the boutique property, pick up your Disney park tickets or MagicBands, download the My Disney Experience app, and pre-book Lightning Lane selections for the week. Cool off at the resort pool to recover from travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Shopping Evening — Head to Disney Springs (free admission, ~10–15 min from most Lake Buena Vista hotels) for a relaxed first evening. Browse the World of Disney store, enjoy live entertainment on the waterfront, and ease into the Disney atmosphere without the intensity of a full park day.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the airport before landing or snack on the plane — no breakfast scheduled on-property.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the resort check-in area or the hotel's casual café/lobby bar once settled.
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — mid-range waterfront dining with fresh seafood, steaks, and burgers; great ambiance for a first night. Budget ~$25–45 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Prioritize rest and logistics today. Set Lightning Lane Multi Pass bookings for tomorrow's Magic Kingdom visit as soon as you connect to Wi-Fi. June weather in Orlando is hot and humid (90°F/32°C+) with afternoon thunderstorms common — pack ponchos and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park — Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM; arrive by 8:30 AM for early entry if staying on-site). Head immediately to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train using Lightning Lane. Ride Peter Pan's Flight, 'it's a small world', and The Haunted Mansion before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Continued — After lunch, experience Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Jungle Cruise. Use Lightning Lane passes strategically for the afternoon rush. Take a mid-afternoon break at the resort (on-site guests can return and come back) if energy dips — this is the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom Nighttime Spectacular — Return to Magic Kingdom for the evening. Secure a viewing spot 45–60 minutes early for the 'Disney Enchantment' or 'Happily Ever After' fireworks show over Cinderella Castle. Ride any remaining attractions with shorter evening wait times before the show.

meals.breakfast: Resort hotel breakfast or quick grab-and-go from the resort's marketplace to fuel up before rope drop.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House (Liberty Square) — counter-service with clam chowder, lobster rolls, and sandwiches in a charming nautical setting. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Fantasyland) — mid-range, immersive Beauty and the Beast-themed dining. Book well in advance via My Disney Experience. Budget ~$20–35 per adult for dinner.

day_by_day.notes: This is the Magic Kingdom Park Full Day Adventure experience. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a refillable water bottle — free ice water is available at any quick-service location. Lightning Lane Multi Pass is highly recommended for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and Tiana's Bayou Adventure.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Arrive at EPCOT for rope drop (~9:00 AM). Start in Future World/World Discovery to ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind and Test Track early before lines grow. Then transition to the World Showcase as it opens at 11:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Exploration — Stroll through the 11 country pavilions around World Showcase Lagoon. Sample authentic dishes and snacks from Mexico, Japan, France, Morocco, and Italy. Experience Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France pavilion (use Lightning Lane) and the Gran Fiesta Tour in Mexico. Explore cultural exhibits and artisan demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT Harmonious Nighttime Show — Stay for EPCOT's spectacular nighttime lagoon show featuring massive floating set pieces, fountains, fire, and projections. Find a great viewing spot along the World Showcase promenade. Enjoy a final country pavilion or two before the show begins.

meals.breakfast: Quick-service breakfast at the resort before heading out.
meals.lunch: World Showcase grazing — try a crêpe from France (~$8), tacos from Mexico (~$12), and a school bread from Norway (~$6). Budget ~$20–30 total for a progressive lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo (Japan Pavilion) — mid-range teppanyaki-style Japanese dining with entertaining tableside cooking. Book in advance. Budget ~$30–45 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: This is the EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour experience. EPCOT is best experienced at a leisurely pace — don't rush the World Showcase. Bring cash or load a Disney gift card for smaller food-stand purchases. The International Food & Wine Festival runs seasonally and may overlap with your June visit.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Hollywood Studios — Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — Arrive at rope drop for Hollywood Studios (~9:00 AM, or use Early Theme Park Entry if eligible). Head straight to Galaxy's Edge. Book a reservation for Savi's Workshop (Handbuilt Lightsabers, ~$249.99) or Droid Depot (~$119.99) — these require advance reservations. Ride Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance first thing using Lightning Lane Individual (book at 7:00 AM sharp on the app).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hollywood Studios Broader Exploration — After Galaxy's Edge, explore Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run, then head to Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers. Experience Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster in Sunset Boulevard. Catch a showing of Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Fantasmic! Nighttime Show — Hollywood Studios' iconic nighttime spectacular featuring Mickey Mouse, water screens, fire, and beloved Disney villains. Arrive 60–90 minutes early for the best seats in the 6,900-seat Hollywood Hills Amphitheater. Enjoy the park atmosphere until closing.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the resort before an early departure for rope drop.
meals.lunch: Ronto Roasters (Galaxy's Edge) — try the Ronto Wrap (roasted pork and grilled sausage in pita bread). Budget ~$13–15 per item. Very popular and authentic to the Star Wars theme.
meals.dinner: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant — mid-range counter-service style dining in a retro drive-in movie theater setting showing classic sci-fi clips. Budget ~$20–30 per adult. Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: This is the Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Immersive Experience day. Lightsaber building at Savi's Workshop books out weeks in advance — confirm your reservation before arrival. Wear comfortable clothes as June heat in Galaxy's Edge can be intense. The Star Wars theming is fully immersive — cast members stay in character throughout.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom — Safari & Avatar Experience — Arrive at rope drop (~8:00 AM, one of the earliest-opening parks). Head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride) using Lightning Lane Individual. Then experience Na'vi River Journey for a calmer but visually stunning boat ride through bioluminescent rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kilimanjaro Safari & Animal Kingdom Exploration — Head to Africa for the Kilimanjaro Safari — aim for early afternoon when animals are often more active in shaded areas. See lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and more in naturalistic habitats. Explore Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail on foot. Visit Asia for Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (prepare to get wet!).
day_by_day.evening: Rivers of Light / Tree of Life Awakenings — As dusk falls, watch the Tree of Life come alive with projected animal spirits — a free, magical experience that occurs every few minutes. Catch the Rivers of Light nighttime show at the amphitheater if running. The park typically closes earlier than others, so plan to depart by 9:00–10:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast or grab a snack at the park entrance upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue (Discovery Island) — one of Disney's best quick-service options with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken with a beautiful waterfront seating area. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant (Asia) — mid-range Asian fusion restaurant with pan-seared salmon, Mongolian beef, and dim sum. Great atmosphere. Budget ~$25–40 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: This is the Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience day. Flight of Passage Lightning Lane Individual sells out by 7:00 AM — book the moment the window opens. Bring a change of clothes or a poncho for Kali River Rapids. Animal Kingdom is a walking-intensive park — comfortable footwear is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Resort Relaxation & Leisure Morning — Take a well-deserved slow morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort, use the pool, or explore your boutique hotel's amenities. This recovery day is important mid-trip to recharge energy for the final days. Optionally, visit a Disney resort hotel lobby for free (like the Grand Floridian or Polynesian) to enjoy the theming and atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT or Magic Kingdom Return Visit / Park Hopping — Use this afternoon for a park hop to catch any missed attractions. Recommended: Return to Magic Kingdom for Tiana's Bayou Adventure, the updated TRON Lightcycle / Run (book Lightning Lane early), or any favorites you want to re-ride. Alternatively, explore EPCOT's Future World area more deeply.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment — Return to Disney Springs for a festive Saturday evening. Browse unique shops like Uniqlo, Star Wars Galactic Outpost, and the LEGO Store. Enjoy live music at the outdoor stages. This is a great opportunity for souvenir shopping and a relaxed final full-evening out.

meals.breakfast: Resort hotel full breakfast — treat yourself to a sit-down meal at the boutique hotel's restaurant or a nearby resort dining location.
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs or a casual poolside lunch at the resort. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: STK Orlando at Disney Springs — upscale-casual steakhouse with a lively atmosphere, great cocktails, and excellent steaks. A mid-to-upper-range splurge for a special evening. Budget ~$45–65 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is one of the busiest days at Disney parks — consider using this as a lighter day and avoiding the most crowded parks. Disney Springs is always free to enter and a great Saturday evening destination. Use any remaining Lightning Lane credits wisely if park hopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final Park Morning — Magic Kingdom or EPCOT Farewell — Choose your favorite park for one last magical morning. If returning to Magic Kingdom, ride any must-do attractions you missed or want to experience again. Purchase last-minute souvenirs inside the park. Take photos in front of Cinderella Castle for a memorable farewell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Check-Out & Final Experiences — Check out of the boutique stay (standard checkout ~11:00 AM; request late checkout if available). Store luggage with the bell desk and use remaining afternoon time for a final Disney Springs visit, resort pool dip, or relaxed stroll. If your flight departs late, Disney's resort luggage storage allows you to enjoy the property until departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Head to Orlando International Airport with ample time. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight for security. Reflect on an amazing week at Walt Disney World!

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a quick grab-and-go from the hotel marketplace — fuel up for the final morning park visit.
meals.lunch: Quick-service in the park or a final Disney Springs lunch. Try Earl of Sandwich at Disney Springs for a quick, affordable, and delicious farewell meal. Budget ~$10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the resort before heading to MCO. Alternatively, pack snacks for the flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight time and arrange transportation to MCO in advance — rideshare, Disney's Magical Express alternative (Mears Connect), or rental car return. Orlando traffic on Sunday afternoons can be heavy — budget extra travel time. Don't forget to check all hotel rooms for left-behind items before checkout!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Disney World, Orlando, Florida Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day Adventure
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring the iconic Magic Kingdom, riding classics like Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and the Haunted Mansion. Watch the Festival of Fantasy parade and end the night with the spectacular Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle.
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Immersive Experience
experiences.description: Step into the world of Star Wars at Hollywood Studios' Galaxy's Edge. Build your own lightsaber at Savi's Workshop, pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, and experience the thrilling Rise of the Resistance ride. Enjoy themed food and drinks at Oga's Cantina for a fully immersive experience.

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore EPCOT's World Showcase, a living showcase of 11 countries around the lagoon. Sample authentic cuisines from Mexico, Japan, France, Morocco, and more. Enjoy cultural performances, artisan demonstrations, and the breathtaking EPCOT Forever nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon.
experiences.location: EPCOT World Showcase, Future World, Orlando

experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience
experiences.description: Embark on the Kilimanjaro Safari to see real African wildlife including lions, elephants, and giraffes. Then journey to Pandora – The World of Avatar for the breathtaking Flight of Passage ride and the serene Na'vi River Journey. Explore the lush, immersive landscapes and enjoy themed dining at Satu'li Canteen.
experiences.location: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Pandora – The World of Avatar, Orlando

experiences.name: Disney Springs Dining & Shopping Evening
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed evening at Disney Springs, Disney's free-admission entertainment district. Enjoy world-class dining at restaurants like The BOATHOUSE or Morimoto Asia, browse unique Disney merchandise and boutique shops, catch live entertainment, and let the kids enjoy the interactive water fountains and splash pad area.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Arrange private luxury transfer from Orlando International Airport to your boutique stay at Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Settle into your suite and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Leisure: After check-in, take a leisurely stroll around the Magic Kingdom resort area. Visit the iconic Main Street, U.S.A. for light browsing and souvenir shopping. If energy permits, enjoy a relaxed ride on the Walt Disney World Railroad or the classic Carousel of Progress as a gentle introduction to the park.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day Adventure (Evening Portion): Head into Magic Kingdom for the spectacular evening experience. Secure Lightning Lane Premier Pass reservations for Tomorrowland's Space Mountain and Fantasyland's Seven Dwarfs Mine Train. Cap the night with the breathtaking 'Disney Enchantment' fireworks spectacular over Cinderella Castle.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street, U.S.A. — a charming, upscale American bistro with white-tablecloth service and classic sandwiches, salads, and sundaes with a view of Cinderella Castle
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table — a premium, reservation-required dining experience inside Cinderella Castle offering a prix-fixe menu of filet mignon, pan-seared salmon, and decadent desserts with character meet-and-greets

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Lightning Lane Premier Pass and Cinderella's Royal Table reservations (up to 60 days in advance). Arrange private airport transfer in advance for a seamless luxury arrival. Pack light for the evening park visit — comfortable, stylish resort wear recommended. Stay hydrated as June temperatures in Orlando can reach 90°F+ with high humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day Adventure (Morning): Arrive at Magic Kingdom at rope drop (park opening, typically 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Begin with Fantasyland's most coveted rides — Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and Peter Pan's Flight — before lines build. Explore Adventureland's Pirates of the Caribbean and the Jungle Cruise with a VIP guided tour option for skip-the-line access throughout the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Continued — Thrills & Classics: Tackle Tomorrowland's Space Mountain and TRON Lightcycle / Run (one of the park's newest and most thrilling coasters). Enjoy a mid-afternoon break at the resort's pool or your suite to escape peak heat before returning refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom After Dark: Return for the immersive 'Festival of Fantasy' parade and the 'Happily Ever After' or 'Disney Enchantment' nighttime spectacular. Explore Liberty Square and Frontierland under the magical evening lighting. Enjoy a leisurely walk back to your boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Steakhouse 71 at Disney's Contemporary Resort — an upscale all-day dining restaurant serving a lavish breakfast buffet with made-to-order omelets, prime cuts, and fresh pastries just steps from Magic Kingdom via the resort monorail
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant — dine inside the enchanted Beast's Castle in Fantasyland with a prix-fixe lunch menu featuring French-inspired cuisine including braised pork, croque monsieur, and exquisite desserts
meals.dinner: California Grill at Disney's Contemporary Resort — a rooftop fine-dining gem with panoramic views of Magic Kingdom's fireworks, offering wood-fired sushi, artisan flatbreads, and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book a VIP Tour Guide through Disney's private tour services for the ultimate skip-the-line experience — guides are knowledgeable and provide insider access. California Grill allows guests to step outside on the observation deck during the fireworks with a valid same-day dining reservation. Lightning Lane Premier Pass strongly recommended for TRON Lightcycle / Run.

day_by_day.morning: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Immersive Experience — Morning: Arrive at Hollywood Studios at rope drop for exclusive access to Galaxy's Edge before crowds surge. Begin with the legendary Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run attraction. Head immediately to Savi's Workshop — Handbuilt Lightsabers for a deeply personal, premium lightsaber-building ceremony (reservation required, ~$249.99 per lightsaber). This intimate, story-driven experience is a highlight for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hollywood Studios Exploration: Experience Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance — one of Disney's most technically ambitious and immersive attractions. Explore the Droid Depot to build a custom astromech droid. Visit Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers. Catch an afternoon showing of 'Fantasmic!' if scheduled, or explore the Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster for classic Hollywood thrills.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Shopping Evening: Wind down with a relaxed, upscale evening at Disney Springs. Browse luxury boutiques including UNIQLO, Anthropologie, and Disney flagship stores. Enjoy world-class entertainment and the vibrant waterfront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo (Galaxy's Edge) — an in-universe, immersive quick-service experience with unique themed breakfast items; enjoy it as part of the Star Wars world before the crowds arrive
meals.lunch: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant — a uniquely themed, air-conditioned diner where guests sit in vintage car booths under a starlit sky watching classic sci-fi movie clips; menu features gourmet burgers, lobster mac & cheese, and milkshakes
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia at Disney Springs — celebrity chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship restaurant offering refined Pan-Asian cuisine including Peking duck, sushi platters, and wagyu beef in an elegant, dramatic setting

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop reservations are extremely limited and book out weeks in advance — secure your spot immediately upon booking eligibility. The Droid Depot experience (~$119.99) is an additional premium add-on worth experiencing. Rise of the Resistance frequently has virtual queues or Lightning Lane — check the My Disney Experience app from 7:00 AM. Morimoto Asia accepts reservations via OpenTable.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Morning: Arrive at EPCOT at opening to explore Future World (now World Discovery and World Nature). Experience Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (one of EPCOT's most popular new attractions — Lightning Lane a must) and Soarin' Around the World for a breathtaking aerial journey. Visit the stunning aquarium at The Seas with Nemo & Friends.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Afternoon Tour: Begin the World Showcase loop around World Showcase Lagoon. Sample authentic cuisine, wines, and spirits from pavilions including France, Italy, Japan, Morocco, and Canada. Engage with cultural artisans, live performers, and storytellers. Visit the iconic Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France pavilion for a charming family experience.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT Harmonious Nighttime Spectacular: Stay for EPCOT's 'Harmonious' — one of the largest nighttime spectaculars ever created for a Disney park — featuring floating set pieces, fountains, pyrotechnics, and projections on World Showcase Lagoon. Secure a premium viewing spot near the Italy or America pavilions.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons at The Land Pavilion — a bright, farm-fresh quick-service option with artisan breakfast sandwiches, yogurt parfaits, and fresh-squeezed juices inside EPCOT's lush greenhouse pavilion
meals.lunch: Tutto Italia Ristorante (Italy Pavilion) — an elegant, reservation-recommended Italian restaurant serving authentic Roman cuisine including housemade pastas, risotto, and tiramisu with a charming piazza atmosphere
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul (France Pavilion) — EPCOT's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant, located above the France pavilion, offering classic haute French cuisine including foie gras, duck confit, and soufflés with an award-winning wine list and views of the lagoon

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase officially opens at 11:00 AM while Future World areas open earlier — plan accordingly. The EPCOT Food & Wine Festival (typically August–November) or Flower & Garden Festival (March–July) may overlap with your visit, offering additional premium culinary experiences and special tastings. Monsieur Paul is one of Disney's most difficult reservations — book 60 days in advance at exactly 6:00 AM EST.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience — Morning: Arrive at Animal Kingdom at rope drop for the Kilimanjaro Safari — the experience is most magical in the early morning when animals are most active. Witness lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and cheetahs in a stunning 110-acre savanna setting. Follow with Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for close-up wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pandora — The World of Avatar Afternoon: Immerse yourself in the bioluminescent world of Pandora. Experience Avatar Flight of Passage — widely considered one of Disney's greatest attractions — a soaring, breathtaking banshee ride over Pandora's landscape. Explore Na'vi River Journey for a serene, visually stunning float through a mystical rainforest. Take time to explore Pandora's incredible environmental details and unique food and beverage offerings.
day_by_day.evening: Animal Kingdom Evening & Resort Relaxation: Enjoy the 'Rivers of Light' nighttime spectacular at Animal Kingdom (if available) or the atmospheric Tree of Life Awakenings — a mesmerizing projection show on the park's iconic centerpiece. Return to your boutique resort for a luxurious evening of spa services or pool relaxation.

meals.breakfast: Boma — Flavors of Africa at Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge — even as a non-lodge guest, this celebrated breakfast buffet is worth the short drive, featuring African-inspired dishes including bobotie, pap, fresh exotic fruits, and an extraordinary selection of pastries
meals.lunch: Tiffins Restaurant at Animal Kingdom — Disney's most artistically sophisticated table-service restaurant, featuring globally inspired cuisine including whole-roasted cauliflower, sustainable seafood, and braised short rib in an elegant gallery-like setting adorned with original artwork
meals.dinner: Jiko — The Cooking Place at Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge — an AAA Four Diamond Award-winning restaurant offering wood-fired African-inspired cuisine including maize-crusted filet mignon, oak-grilled salmon, and one of the largest selections of South African wines in the United States

day_by_day.notes: Avatar Flight of Passage Lightning Lane is absolutely essential — this ride consistently has 2–3 hour standby waits. Book at 7:00 AM sharp on the My Disney Experience app. Tiffins is also one of Disney's best kept secrets for fine dining — reservations recommended. Jiko requires a short drive or Minnie Van service to Animal Kingdom Lodge — arrange transportation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Universal Orlando Resort — Optional Premium Day Trip (or EPCOT/Hollywood Studios Revisit): For guests wishing to venture beyond Disney, a morning visit to Universal's Epic Universe (opening 2025) or Islands of Adventure offers world-class thrills including The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Alternatively, return to a favorite Disney park for any missed experiences or to revisit top attractions with a more relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Spa & Resort Afternoon: Book a half-day treatment at the Senses — A Disney Spa at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa (accessible via monorail). Indulge in a couples' massage, hydrotherapy treatments, and premium facial services. Follow with a relaxing afternoon at your boutique resort's pool with cabana service.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Farewell Shopping & Entertainment Evening: Return to Disney Springs for final luxury shopping — pick up premium Disney collectibles, artwork from the Disney Fine Art Gallery, and bespoke gifts. Enjoy live entertainment at the waterfront amphitheater and a final memorable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grand Floridian Café at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort — a refined, Victorian-inspired café serving a lavish breakfast including eggs Benedict, lobster omelets, and freshly baked pastries in an elegant setting steps from the resort's marina
meals.lunch: Paddlefish at Disney Springs — a stunning three-story restaurant aboard a reimagined riverboat, serving premium seafood including Maine lobster, oysters on the half shell, and market-fresh fish with panoramic waterfront views
meals.dinner: STK Orlando at Disney Springs — a modern steakhouse offering USDA prime-aged cuts, wagyu beef, and an extensive cocktail program in a sophisticated, high-energy atmosphere with live DJ entertainment

day_by_day.notes: Senses Spa reservations should be made well in advance — treatments book quickly, especially on weekends. The Grand Floridian is accessible from Magic Kingdom via the resort monorail — a scenic and convenient luxury transit option. STK Orlando has a lively weekend atmosphere — ideal for a celebratory final evening dinner. Request a waterfront table at Paddlefish for the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Farewell Magic Kingdom Morning: Spend a final leisurely morning at Magic Kingdom for any last-minute must-do attractions. Revisit personal favorites or explore anything missed earlier in the trip. Pick up final souvenirs on Main Street, U.S.A. and take commemorative photos in front of Cinderella Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-Out & Departure Preparation: Check out of your boutique stay with ample time before departure. Store luggage with the concierge if needed. Arrange private luxury transfer back to Orlando International Airport. Consider a final stop at Disney Springs for any last-minute gifts or a farewell treat.
day_by_day.evening: Departure: Board your return flight having experienced the full magic of Walt Disney World in unparalleled luxury. Reflect on seven extraordinary days of world-class entertainment, dining, and family memories.

meals.breakfast: The Crystal Palace at Magic Kingdom — a beloved Victorian-style buffet restaurant with Winnie the Pooh character dining, offering an elegant spread of carved meats, fresh seafood, pastries, and made-to-order stations for a magical farewell breakfast
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House (Quick-Service Upgrade) — a charming, nautical-themed counter-service spot in Liberty Square offering elevated quick-service options including lobster roll, clam chowder, and fresh salads — perfect for a light, unhurried farewell meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge — Orlando International Airport's premium lounges (including the Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club or Amex Centurion Lounge) offer elevated pre-departure dining and cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for transportation and airport security — Orlando International can be extremely busy on summer Sundays. Use Disney's Magical Express or a pre-arranged private car service for a seamless departure. The Crystal Palace character breakfast is a beloved tradition — book 60 days in advance. Consider purchasing a Disney PhotoPass Memory Maker package before the trip to capture all professional park photos across all 7 days.
